strings.title: The Locked Room Mystery
strings.hint: Who was really writing? Compare the old novel drafts with the novelist's own handwriting. Who could fit through the narrow rooftop window?
strings.solvedText:
The killer: Nadia Sarhan — the literary secretary and ghostwriter.

For nine years, she had written his novels in full in return for a promise that he would reveal her name 'when the time was right.' When he decided to publish the latest novel under his own name and refused to acknowledge her once again, she hid in the study before it was locked. She added a fatal sedative to his whisky, burned the dedication pages that would expose her, then left through the narrow rooftop window. Using a clamp and magnet, she turned the key from outside to make the room appear locked from within.

The evidence against her: magnetic-tool scratches on the lock, the match between the old drafts and her notebooks, and a window opening that only she could fit through.
strings.summary.text: Famous novelist Walid Najm was found dead behind his desk. The room was locked from the inside, with the key still in the lock. Beside him lay the draft of his latest novel; its opening pages had been burned in the fireplace. There was no forced entry, and the only window was a narrow opening onto the roof. Everyone asks the same question: how did the killer leave a locked room?

strings.scene.intro: A room locked from within, with the key in the lock. A nearly empty whisky glass, burned pages in the fireplace, and a narrow rooftop window closed without a latch. Fine, bright scratches on the lock differ from ordinary wear.
strings.scene.photos[0].cap: Study — where the body was found
strings.scene.notes[0]: Key in the inside lock, with fresh magnetic-tool scratches
strings.scene.notes[1]: Fatal sedative residue in the whisky glass
strings.scene.notes[2]: Only the latest novel's introduction and dedication pages were burned
strings.scene.notes[3]: Narrow rooftop window, 38 cm wide, closed without a latch
strings.evidence[0].title: Key and scratched lock
strings.evidence[0].desc: Fine magnetic-tool scratches around the keyhole indicate the key was turned from outside using a magnetized clamp.
strings.evidence[1].title: The whisky glass
strings.evidence[1].desc: Residue from a fatal dose of sedative. No unfamiliar fingerprints; the glass was carefully wiped.
strings.evidence[2].title: The burned pages
strings.evidence[2].desc: The introduction and dedication were specifically burned — the only section Walid wrote in his own hand.
strings.evidence[3].title: Old novel drafts
strings.evidence[3].desc: 14 drafts in a single hand… which does not match Walid Najm's official handwriting samples.
strings.evidence[4].title: The rooftop window
strings.evidence[4].desc: 38 cm wide, with a fresh fabric trace on the outside.
strings.evidence[5].title: The new publishing contract
strings.evidence[5].desc: The latest novel's contract names Walid alone and includes a strict confidentiality clause.
strings.suspects[0].name: George Fahmy
strings.suspects[0].alibi: 'I was at a business dinner until midnight. I have the receipt.'
strings.suspects[0].statement: Walid was my publishing house's treasure. I would not kill the goose that lays the golden eggs. Yes, we argued over the latest novel's royalties, but it was a dispute over numbers, not blood. Ask about his secretary, who knows his novels better than he does. I always joked that she wrote them.
strings.suspects[1].name: Nadia Sarhan
strings.suspects[1].alibi: 'I left the villa at six in the evening, as usual. I was at home alone.'
strings.suspects[1].statement: I am his right hand. I organize his drafts, review his language and know his style by heart. Our relationship is strictly professional. Talk of a ghostwriter insults both him and me. That night, I was tired and went to bed early. No one witnessed that; as you know, I live alone.
strings.suspects[2].name: Rashid Al-Katib
strings.suspects[2].alibi: 'I was signing my book at the city fair in front of a hundred witnesses.'
strings.suspects[2].statement: I hated his writing and despised him personally. I said so in every newspaper. Open hatred does not kill; the person hiding behind a smile does. Ask who could enter his study without knocking.
strings.witnesses[0].name: Umm Salim
strings.witnesses[0].statement: The door was locked, with the key in the lock on the inside. I have known that lock's sound for ten years. But when it was broken open that morning, its ring sounded strange… as though something had changed inside it.
strings.witnesses[1].name: The engineer next door
strings.witnesses[1].statement: The study lights went out at 22:30, but a faint light, like a phone screen, kept moving behind the curtain for about a quarter of an hour afterward.
strings.witnesses[2].name: Newspaper delivery worker
strings.witnesses[2].statement: Around five in the morning, I saw a slender shape come down the rear roof ladder and walk along the wall. I thought it was a large cat… then it walked like a person.
strings.folders[0].name: Incident reports
strings.folders[0].docs[0].title: Housekeeper's report
strings.folders[0].docs[0].body: The caller reported being unable to open the study since morning, with no response from the owner. She requested that the door be forced in the presence of police.
strings.folders[1].name: Forensic evidence
strings.folders[1].docs[0].title: Lock report
strings.folders[1].docs[0].body: Fresh magnetic-tool scratches around the keyhole indicate that the key was turned from outside with a magnetized tool. The room was not actually locked from within.
strings.folders[1].docs[1].title: Toxicology report
strings.folders[1].docs[1].body: A fatal sedative dissolved in whisky. Death between 22:00 and 23:00. No resistance.
strings.folders[2].name: Interviews
strings.folders[2].docs[0].title: Publisher interview
strings.folders[2].docs[0].body: Produced a dinner receipt and witnesses. Repeated his suggestion that the novels had shown 'a feminine sensibility' for years.
strings.folders[2].docs[1].title: Nadia interview
strings.folders[2].docs[1].body: Extremely calm. Denied any editorial role beyond organizing material. When asked about the rooftop window, she volunteered its exact dimensions in centimeters without being asked for them.
strings.folders[2].docs[2].title: Rashid interview
strings.folders[2].docs[2].body: His presence at the book fair is confirmed. Gave investigators a list of those 'who know the secret of Walid's study,' with the secretary at the top.
strings.folders[3].name: Records
strings.folders[3].docs[0].title: Handwriting sample record
strings.folders[3].docs[0].body: The handwriting in the 14 drafts does not match Walid's official contract handwriting. It closely matches Nadia's notebooks.
strings.folders[3].docs[1].title: Villa gate record
strings.folders[3].docs[1].body: Nadia's departure is logged at 18:02… but her car is not recorded leaving the villa's street until 05:10 the next morning.
strings.folders[4].name: Classified files
strings.folders[4].docs[0].title: Messages about the deferred promise
strings.folders[4].docs[0].body: Messages recovered from Walid's computer show Nadia demanding to be named as co-author. He keeps delaying: 'After this novel… as usual.'
strings.folders[4].docs[1].title: Movement reconstruction report
strings.folders[4].docs[1].body: Reconstruction shows that, among the suspects, only Nadia can fit through the 38 cm window opening. The fabric trace outside matches her coat.
strings.reports[0].title: Locked room report
strings.reports[0].author: Scene examination team
strings.reports[0].body: The inside lock was a trick: the key was turned magnetically from outside, and the killer left through the rooftop window. The crime was planned by someone who knew every inch of the room.
strings.reports[1].title: Literary analysis report
strings.reports[1].author: Text comparison expert
strings.reports[1].body: The stylistic fingerprint of the later novels differs radically from Walid's early articles and matches a free-writing sample taken from his secretary.
strings.notes[0].text: The room was not locked from within — look for who left, not who entered
strings.notes[1].text: Burning the dedication destroys a name… whose?
